title: Subdivision 126-A roll-over — marriage or relationship breakdown
summary: Automatic CGT roll-over where a CGT asset is transferred between spouses or former spouses because of a marriage or relationship breakdown — under a court order, approved maintenance agreement, binding financial agreement, arbitration award or binding written agreement. The transferor's gain or loss is disregarded and the transferee inherits the cost base (or pre-CGT status). Applies to individuals (s 126-5) and companies/trustees (s 126-15), with main residence consequences to check. Subsection coverage: operative 126-5(1)-(8), 126-15(1)-(5), 126-20(1)-(2), 126-25(1)-(2), 118-178(1)-(2), 118-180(1)-(2) mapped to nodes; no machinery/transitional exclusions.

nodes.label: A marriage or relationship breaks down and a CGT event happens involving you and your spouse or former spouse
nodes.body: Subdivision 126-A gives an automatic roll-over (no choice needed) where a CGT asset is transferred between spouses or former spouses because of the breakdown. It applies to individuals (s 126-5) and to companies or trustees (s 126-15) that transfer assets to a spouse or former spouse of another individual.

statute.title: CGT event involving company or trustee

nodes.label: A CGT event happens because of a court order, maintenance agreement, financial agreement, arbitration award or binding written agreement
nodes.body: The trigger event must happen because of: (a) a court order under the Family Law Act 1975 or a State/Territory/foreign law relating to relationship breakdowns; (b) a maintenance agreement approved by a court under s 87 of the FLA; (d)/(da) a binding financial agreement under Part VIIIA (s 90G) or Part VIIIAB (s 90UJ) of the FLA; (e) an arbitration award under s 13H of the FLA; or (f) a written agreement binding under a State/Territory/foreign breakdown law that prevents court orders (s 126-5(1)).

nodes.label: Is the transferee a current spouse or a former spouse?
nodes.body:
The applicable relief depends on whether the transferee is a current spouse or a former spouse:
- *Current spouse (not separated or reconciled)*: The transferor may be able to choose to disregard the gain under the *spouse transfer exemption* in ss 118-178 and 118-180 (main residence context — gain/loss disregarded entirely for a dwelling). These provisions apply to transfers to a spouse (not just former spouse) and are not limited to relationship breakdown situations.
- *Former spouse (separated/divorced)*: The automatic roll-over under Subdivision 126-A applies to transfers to a former spouse because of a relationship breakdown (ss 126-5(1), 126-15(1)). The transferee inherits the transferor's cost base.
The key distinction: ss 118-178/118-180 provide an *exemption* (gain/loss disregarded entirely) but only for main residence dwellings transferred between spouses. Subdivision 126-A provides a *roll-over* (cost-base carry-over) for any CGT asset transferred to a former spouse because of a breakdown.

statute.title: CGT event involving company or trustee
Acquisition from company or trust on breakdown

nodes.label: Is the CGT event a disposal case (A1 or B1) or a creation case (D1, D2, D3 or F1)?
nodes.body: Only CGT events A1 and B1 (disposal) and D1, D2, D3 and F1 (creation) are relevant (s 126-5(2)). Other CGT events do not qualify for the roll-over.

nodes.label: If the transfer is under a financial agreement (d)/(da) or a binding written agreement (f): are the s 126-25 conditions met?
nodes.body: The roll-over is not available for transfers under paragraphs (d), (da) or (f) unless, at the time of the trigger event: the spouses or former spouses are separated, there is no reasonable likelihood of cohabitation being resumed, and the event happened for reasons directly connected with the breakdown (s 126-25). Separation is determined as under s 48 of the Family Law Act 1975 (as affected by ss 49-50). Court orders and approved maintenance agreements do not need these conditions.

statute.title: Conditions for the purposes of subsections 126-5(3A) and 126-15(5)

nodes.label: Is the asset trading stock of the transferor, or does title fail to pass (B1)?
nodes.body: There is no roll-over if the CGT asset is trading stock of the transferor, or (for CGT event B1) title in the asset does not pass to the transferee at or before the end of the agreement (s 126-5(3)).

nodes.label: Is the transferor an individual, or a company or trustee?
nodes.body: For an individual transferor the consequences are in s 126-5(4)-(8). For a company or trustee transferor the same consequences apply (s 126-15(1)), with additional cost base adjustments for other assets the entity owns (s 126-15(2)-(4)) and special rules if the transferor was a CFC or non-resident trust (s 126-20).

nodes.label: Disposal case or creation case?
nodes.body: Disposal: CGT events A1 or B1. Creation: CGT events D1, D2, D3 or F1. The cost base consequences differ (s 126-5(5)-(8)).

nodes.label: Disposal of a post-CGT asset: the transferee's cost base is the transferor's cost base
nodes.body: For a disposal case where the transferor acquired the asset on or after 20 September 1985, the first element of the asset's cost base (and reduced cost base) in the transferee's hands is the transferor's cost base at the time the transferee acquired it (s 126-5(5)). Special indexation rules apply (Division 114).

nodes.label: Disposal of a pre-CGT asset: the transferee is taken to have acquired it before 20 September 1985
nodes.body: For a disposal case where the transferor acquired the asset before 20 September 1985, the transferee is taken to have acquired it before that day, so gains are generally disregarded on a later disposal (s 126-5(6); Division 149 removes the exemption in some cases).

nodes.label: Disposal of a collectable or personal use asset: the transferee is taken to have acquired one
nodes.body: Where the transferor disposed of a collectable or personal use asset, the transferee is taken to have acquired a collectable or personal use asset respectively (s 126-5(7)) — so capital losses from collectables can only offset collectable gains (s 108-10) and personal use asset losses are disregarded (s 108-20).

nodes.label: Creation case: the transferee's cost base is the transferor's expenditure per the s 126-5(8) table
nodes.body: For D1 the cost base is the incidental costs the transferor incurred relating to the trigger event; D2 the expenditure to grant the option; D3 the expenditure to grant the right; F1 the expenditure on the grant, renewal or extension of the lease (s 126-5(8)). The reduced cost base is worked out similarly. Expenditure can include giving property (s 103-5).

nodes.label: Company or trustee transferor: same roll-over, plus cost base adjustments to other assets
nodes.body: The s 126-5 consequences apply (s 126-15(1)). Where an entity (including the transferee) owned another CGT asset — shares in the company, a loan to it, or an indirect interest; or an interest/unit in the trust, a loan to the trustee, or an indirect interest — the cost base and reduced cost base of that other asset are reduced by an amount reflecting the fall in its market value because of the trigger event (s 126-15(2)-(3)). If the owner is also the transferee, the cost base is then increased by amounts included in assessable income because of the trigger event (s 126-15(4)).

nodes.label: Was the company/trustee transferor a CFC or a non-resident trust estate?
nodes.body: Where the transferor was a CFC or a non-resident trust estate and the roll-over asset was not taxable Australian property (ignoring residency assumptions), a subsequent CGT event on the asset is modified under Division 7 of Part X or Subdivision D of Division 6AAA of the ITAA 1936 (s 126-20).

statute.title: Subsequent CGT event happening to roll-over asset where transferor was a CFC or a non-resident trust

nodes.label: Main residence exemption: ss 118-178/118-180 apply — transferor's period of ownership and use carried over to transferee
nodes.body:
A roll-over under Subdivision 126-A can affect the transferee's main residence exemption:
- *Section 118-178* (previous roll-over under Subdivision 126-A): Where the transferee acquired a dwelling from a former partner under a 126-A roll-over, the main residence exemption applies as if the transferee's ownership interest commenced when the former partner's interest commenced, and as if the dwelling was the transferee's main residence for the same period it was the former partner's main residence.
- *Section 118-180* (acquisition from company/trust on breakdown): Where a dwelling is acquired from a company or trustee under a 126-A roll-over, the transferee is treated as owning the interest during the period the company/trustee owned it, but it cannot be treated as the transferee's main residence during that period.
These sections effectively *carry forward* the transferor's main residence history to the transferee.

statute.title: Acquisition from company or trust on breakdown

nodes.label: Roll-over applies — the transferor's gain or loss is disregarded and cost bases re-base into the transferee
nodes.body: The transferor's capital gain or capital loss from the trigger event is disregarded (s 126-5(4) for individuals, s 126-15(1) for companies/trustees). The transferee inherits the transferor's cost base (or pre-CGT status) and, for creation cases, the transferor's expenditure. For transfers to a current spouse involving a main residence dwelling, ss 118-178 and 118-180 carry the transferor's ownership and use history over to the transferee.

nodes.label: No roll-over — the CGT event runs normally
nodes.body: If the transfer is not under a qualifying instrument, the s 126-25 conditions are not met, the asset is trading stock, or title does not pass, the transferor is taxed on any capital gain from the CGT event under the usual rules (CGT event A1, s 104-10). Note: the spouse transfer exemption in ss 118-178/118-180 may still apply to current spouse transfers of a main residence dwelling, even if the 126-A roll-over is not available.
